In progress, 2026-10-14

Notes on the chord-change lessons built in this session. Nothing here is committed unless git log says so.

What exists

Twelve lessons now share one look: numbered steps, each a chord chart (TuneChart) with a staff under it and the Backing Track band, then usually a builder and an ear test.

Lesson File Notes
Blues changes lessons/blues-changes.qmd Existing. Now has a grand staff under every chart. Hand-written script.
C, Am, F, G lessons/pop-changes.qmd Hand-written script, same shape as the blues one.
Four-chord loops lessons/four-chord-loops.qmd Hand-written script. Eight loops, builder, ear test.
Cadences lessons/cadences.qmd Engine. Plagal taught as the “fake” cadence (the argument is in section 4).
Guide tones lessons/guide-tones.qmd Engine. Staff shows a single line; the band’s piano plays it.
Minor changes lessons/minor-changes.qmd Engine. Written in A minor (tonic 9).
Borrowed chords lessons/borrowed-chords.qmd Engine.
Turnarounds lessons/turnarounds.qmd Engine.
Reharmonizing lessons/reharmonize.qmd Engine. Ode to Joy with four sets of chords, melody played by the band.
Pop changes for guitar / piano / bass lessons/pop-changes-guitar.qmd, -piano, -bass Engine, with fretboard, keyboard or bass diagrams.

The nine newest .qmd files were generated by a script (not kept in the repo) that pasted the same style block, bottom strip and script tags into each, then a ChordLesson.init({...}) config. To change the shared page furniture, edit each .qmd or write the generator again. To change behaviour, edit the engine.

Shared code

  • apps/shared/lessons/chord-staff.js (LessonChordStaff): the staff under a chart. Modes: chords (grand staff, block chords and bass note), third, seventh, guide (one line), bass (bass clef). Also describe(sym, transpose, flats) for the diagrams.
  • apps/shared/lessons/chord-lesson.js (ChordLesson): steps, builder, ear tests, key strip, diagrams (guitar, piano, bass), and a tune’s melody above the chart. Config is documented in its header.
  • apps/shared/lessons/tunes.js: added BluesTunes.ode (key C), and inKey now uses a tune’s own key instead of assuming F.
  • apps/shared/tune-chart.js: bars with a chord under a third of the bar wide are drawn smaller (tc-tight), which fixed the cramped numerals in ~/Desktop/cramped.png. Script version is ?v=31 in the lessons that load it.

Tests

tests/band/lessons/loops.cdp.js (“CHORD LESSONS OK”): every new page has the right number of staves, the key menu respells them, the sounding bar lights on chart and staff, the ear tests give a verdict and reveal the chart, the guide-tone staff has one note per chord, the guitar lesson draws four diagrams, tight bars get tc-tight. tests/band/lessons/blues.cdp.js still passes. Setup is in tests/band/README.md (render the pages into tests/band/lead/site/lessons, serve on port 8500).

What nobody has listened to

All of it. I checked layout in screenshots and that the pages run without errors, but not how it sounds. In particular:

  • the guide-tone lines played by the band’s piano (does the melody sit well over the comping?);
  • the “busy” setting in the reharmonizing lesson, and whether the chords really fit Ode to Joy note for note;
  • the minor, borrowed and turnaround lessons in each feel (Piano ballad, Acoustic strum, Motown, Medium swing, Bossa nova);
  • the staff lighting during playback on a phone-width screen.

Things to check

  • Song names in four-chord-loops.qmd: Let It Be, No Woman, No Cry, Don’t Stop Believin’, Zombie, Despacito, Stand by Me, I Got Rhythm, Louie Louie, Wild Thing, Sweet Home Alabama, Hit the Road Jack were written from memory.
  • The cadences lesson states a position (plagal is not a cadence) and cites William Caplin’s Classical Form for it. Please check the citation against the book before it is relied on.
  • Guitar diagrams come from the band’s open-shape library, which ignores the note after a slash. G/B shows the G shape. The lesson says so.
  • “Mario cadence” in borrowed-chords.qmd (♭VI–♭VII–I) is a popular name, not a textbook one.
  • Prose in the nine newer lessons was written in one pass and read only by me.

Not done

  • No lesson links yet from the blues lessons to the new ones.
  • The instrument lessons stop at secondary dominants. No two-fives or builder.
  • The guitar and bass lesson pages are long (a diagram per chord per step); they may want a “show one chord at a time” control.
  • The generator script should be kept in scripts/ if the nine pages are going to be edited in bulk.
  • Quiz questions pick answers at random, and the second cadence question uses my own wording for how each ending “feels”. Rewrite it in your own words.

In progress, 2026-10-14: Chord Entry pickups, syllables, Backing Track hand-off

A separate session from the lessons above. Nothing committed.

Done

  • Backing Track → melody entry. tools/_backing-track.qmd: a button “Open in the melody entry tool” (#bt-mel-entry) in the Melody panel. It opens chord-entry.html#from=tune&d=… the way the lyrics site’s Band panel does, with the changes, tempo, style, title and the melody so far (gridMelody). A pickup in front of bar 1 is not sent; the panel says so.
  • Pickups between sections (tools/_chord-entry.qmd):
    • On loading a .cho, the words before a section’s first chord (“Gone a[Eb]way”) become its pickup (lyr[k].lead), if the last bar of the section before has notes to spare (pickOf, choSections records pick). Before this, the pickup count was lost on every reload.
    • If there are no notes for those words, the load note says so (“…has no notes for it: record Verse 3 with the pickup played in the count-in”).
    • mergeTake: a take to the end of a section keeps the next section’s pickup notes at the end of its last bar, unless the take played into them. (Re-recording the Bridge used to wipe Verse 3’s “Lat-er”.)
  • Syllables in the words box. The first lyric box (“The words, by syllable”) shows the words hyphenated once the dictionary has loaded (splitWords, once per section, lyr[k].split). Hyphens there drive the drafts. The Split into syllables button (#ce-words-split) splits typed or pasted words that have no hyphen yet. Words split only by their vowels are listed in the warning line.
  • Count-off menu (#ce-countin beside Hear it in the Check panel: 1, 2 or 4 bars, default 1, kept in localStorage ceCountIn). It sets the band player’s countIn (player clamp raised from 2 to 4) for Hear it and band takes, and the page’s own click for click takes (sess.count = bars x one bar’s beats, accent on every bar of the count-off). The take engine is unchanged: only the last count-off bar is read (pickup notes), earlier ones are dropped as before. 4 bars are “1 2 3 4” bars; only a count-off of 2 keeps the half-speed first bar. chord-entry.js tag is now ?v=10 (its content did not change; the page and player.js?v=122 did). Test: tests/band/entry/countin.cdp.js (“COUNT-IN OK”).

Tests

tests/band/entry/pickup.cdp.js now covers a save and reload, a re-take of the section before, and a split fixed in the box. Two of its asserts were loosened (whether the held note is drawn tied depends on timing). songfile.cdp.js and sections.cdp.js compare the words with hyphens taken out.

Passing: pickup, songfile, sections, take. Not passing yet: melody-bt, side, entry. They load the Backing Track page and stop on “abc-tune.js needs /apps/shared/abc-core.js loaded before it” (the abc-core.js change from another session). Re-render tools/backing-track.qmd into tests/band/lead/site and run them again. Resolved (ABC session): re-rendered; melody-bt, side and entry now pass.

One shared ABC parser, toward a notation system with MIDI and audio entry (a separate session)

The goal, agreed in chat: one notation system built from the tune, tonal and rhythm assessments, Song Builder and Chord/Melody Entry. You set the parameters first (key, meter, allowed rhythm cells, strictness), then enter by MIDI, tapping or microphone, and a decoder ranks what you might have meant (an extended MelodyDwim). Microphone input is built last, but the design allows for it from the start: every event carries a confidence, and noisy MIDI stands in for the microphone in tests.

Done, not committed (the tests/abc entry under “Other people’s changes” above is this): - apps/shared/abc-core.js (AbcCore): tokenizer, header fields, key signatures, note→MIDI, chord symbols. - apps/assessment/abc-pitch.js, apps/rhythm-assessment/abc-rhythm.js, apps/tune-assessment/abc-tune.js are now thin wrappers over it, with exactly the old output. Each throws a clear error if abc-core.js was not loaded first. - <script src="/apps/shared/abc-core.js?v=1"> before the parser in 13 .qmd pages (seven practice pages, tools/_backing-track, tools/_chord-entry, lessons/_blues-kit, blues-changes, four-chord-loops, pop-changes). tests/band/tune/t_score.js and t_oracle.js load it too. One pointer line was added to CLAUDE.md. - Tests: node tests/abc/compare.js → “ABC SAME” (frozen old parsers in tests/abc/baseline/ against the new ones, on every tune, pattern, rhythm and benchmark plus edge cases; also checks every page loads the core first). The test was checked by planting five errors in the core; it catches all of them. SITE=<rendered pages> node tests/abc/pages.cdp.js → “PAGES SAME” (13 pages in headless Chrome, old parsers against new). quarto preview copied everything into _site, and every _site page that loads a parser has the core tag. - Later: re-rendered tools/backing-track.qmd into tests/band/lead/site (its copy predated the core tag); entry/melody-bt, side, entry pass again. Every lesson page in the test site loads the core.

Found, deliberately not fixed (it changes grades): - The tonal assessment grades 53 of the 148 live patterns (pattern-set.js) on the wrong pitches. abc-pitch.js knows only C major and C minor. Any key starting with a letter then “m” (Dm, also Gmix) is read as C minor, and other keys as C major. The staff shows the right key, but grading expects e.g. F where the staff shows F♯ in D. apps/assessment/app.js also assumes C for the key menu names and the resting-tone target (60 + transpose). Fix: grade with AbcCore.keyAccidentals, then rework those two places. Students’ past results were scored the old way.

Next, in order: 1. (Recommended first) fix the tonal key bug above. 2. The event model: { t_on, t_off, pitch candidates, confidence, source }, built on AbcCore.tokens. Keep written events (one per notehead, which the rhythm assessment’s notehead colouring needs) separate from sounding notes (ties merged). 3. The profile schema (key/mode, allowed degrees, meter, subdivision, swing, triplets, RhythmCells vocabulary, strictness). 4. A decoder on MIDI that wraps Chord Entry’s quantizer, plus a noisy-MIDI test helper (jitter, cents drift, merged and split notes). 5. MelodyDwim ranking by profile. 6.
